For in that bread, a story could bloom, and once it bloomed, the eater would understand a truth they hadn’t known they sought.

It spoke without a mouth, in a language woven from wind and wheat. “Baker,” it said, “you give your loaves thought and sweat. From that day, the village traded more than bread. They traded attention. They learned to listen as if listening could bend time, and in bending time, their small world grew large enough to hold one more dream. The oven glowed with a patient star across every season, reminding them that nourishment is not only a meal but a listening heart.
